maria: hey folks — i have a trace id (0af34b9c) from a failed request in prod. what's the fastest way to pull the original request/log lines?
ken: console -> Observability -> Traces. paste the trace id, open the trace, click 'Related logs' on the span you care about. that opens the Logs view filtered by trace. :thumbsup:
ken: if you prefer CLI: `redwoodctl logs query --trace-id 0af34b9c --since 30m --service api` should return the log lines with `trace_id`/`request_id` fields.
olivia: another quick trick: if you have the request headers, look for `x-request-id` — the logs also index on that and it's much faster to grep if the trace sampling missed it.
maria: i don't see the trace in the console search (no results). could sampling be the issue?
david: yup, possible. check whether the request hit an edge router that strips trace headers or hit a private deployment region. also check the trace sampling rate for the service: `infra -> Observability Config -> Trace Sampling` (eng-perms required).
maria: i have the request_id 8f2c1d4a instead. how to map that to logs?
ken: `redwoodctl logs query --request-id 8f2c1d4a --since 1h` or the console Logs -> filter `request_id:8f2c1d4a` works. example: 
```
redwoodctl logs query --request-id 8f2c1d4a --json | jq -r '.[] | "[\(.timestamp)] \(.service) \(.level) \(.message)"'
```
maria: ran that, returned nothing. permissions maybe? i'm on the default eng read role.
ken: you need `logs:view` on prod. ask ops for `eng:prod-logs` role or run from the shared `debug` machine (has elevated token).
olivia: if CLI returns nothing but the console trace shows spans, open the span and copy the `span.link` — some services write `trace_link=<trace>` instead of `trace_id`. the console "Related logs" handles both.
david: additional diagnostics: check the ingest pipeline health (kafka -> log-processor). sometimes logs are delayed or dropped for big spikes. ping @sre oncall if you suspect ingestion issues.
srebot: [automated] ingestion pipeline status: all consumer groups healthy, lag < 5000, last reprocess: 2026-11-03T14:02:12Z -> https://console.redwood.ai/observability/pipeline/status
maria: thanks — the trace wasn't sampled, but i had the request_id; after getting ops to add the prod-read role i could pull the lines with `redwoodctl`. saved me.
ken: TL;DR cheatsheet:
- Console: Observability > Traces -> paste trace id -> Related logs.
- CLI: `redwoodctl logs query --trace-id <id>` or `--request-id <id>` + `--since`/`--service`.
- If no results: check sampling, permissions, private region routing.
- Use `jq`/`rg` on JSON output to extract fields quickly.
maria: sweet, closing this thread. thanks all :raised_hands:
